title: Three Fridays and One Short Bun
subtitle: 饮食文化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食文化（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）
meta: 主题语境：饮食文化（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）　|　核心词汇：hamburger　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 hamburger 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the cook ① made a hamburger that no customer in the diner would have described, and he said the making was the whole of the Friday. The ② hamburger, meaning the sandwich itself and not the bun, ran three Fridays and stayed undescribed in the book; a hamburger, he said, is the only thing in a diner that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ hamburger in that diner had the same short bun beside it, and the ④ hamburger at the far grill, meaning the patty they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A hamburger, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the cook said the describing is the part that fills three Fridays.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the hamburger was the whole of the matter, meaning the taste and not the sandwich. The ⑥ hamburger, meaning the taste and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; hamburger, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a sandwich and a taste. He said the taste is the part they remember.

By 1984 the ⑦ hamburger had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short bun. The ⑧ hamburger of the whole thing, the cook wrote in November, was one diner and three Fridays of describing; hamburger, he said, is either the patty at the far grill or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ hamburger I remember is the one described in the list, which closed in 1986 and is still described as the quietest in the diner. A ⑩ hamburger, my mother said in 1988, is the only one that improves by being described; every hamburger, she said, is a taste that has agreed to look like a sandwich. She said the taste was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 汉堡包（指餐馆里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 汉堡包（指那份三明治本身，与小圆面包相对）
C. 固定搭配：make a hamburger 做一个汉堡包
D. n. 汉堡包（指留给孩子们学着做的那一个）
E. n. 汉堡（抽象总称，指一家餐馆的汉堡之事）
F. n. 汉堡包（指清单里写到、被记下的那一个）
G. n. 碎牛肉；牛肉饼（指一件事里人人都煎却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 肉饼（抽象总称，指人人都煎却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: made a hamburger that no customer in the diner would have described
The hamburger, meaning the sandwich itself and not the bun
the hamburger at the far grill
the hamburger was the whole of the matter
the hamburger had become a line in a list
The hamburger of the whole thing
A hamburger, my mother said in 1988

answers.why: make a hamburger 意为“做一个汉堡包”，1979 年那位厨师做了餐馆里没有一位顾客肯描述的一个汉堡包。
hamburger 意为“汉堡包”，指那份三明治本身而不是小圆面包，它经过了三个星期五而在簿子上没有被描述。
hamburger 意为“汉堡包”，指餐馆里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一个矮矮的面包。
hamburger 意为“汉堡包”，指最远那张烤架上留给孩子们学着做的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
hamburger 意为“碎牛肉、牛肉饼”，指一件事里人人都煎却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这块肉饼就是那件事的全部。
hamburger 意为“肉饼”，指人人都煎却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个汉堡包，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
hamburger 意为“汉堡包”，指清单里写到、被记下的那一个，到 1984 年这一个成了清单里的一行。
hamburger 意为“汉堡”，厨师十一月写道，整件事的汉堡之事是一家餐馆和三个星期五的描述。
hamburger 意为“汉堡包”，我记得的是清单里描述过的那一个，1986 年卖完了，至今仍被说成餐馆里最安静的一个。
hamburger 为抽象总称，母亲 1988 年说，汉堡包是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的食物。
